entries.grant: Written for Orincard by the team; may be reproduced, parsed, exported and screenshotted without limit inside the project.

evidence.value: Topic phrases and paragraphs typed into tests/fixtures/corpus.json by the Orincard team for T090; no external text was copied into them.

entries.notes: Short original copy that lives inline in the corpus manifest. Kept internal because it is acceptance material, not published writing.

entries.grant: Long-form prose authored in this repository; full rights to parse, render and export.
entries.notes: The guide and legal pages are the project's own publications, so their git history is the provenance record.

entries.grant: Pages Orincard itself serves; fetching them is reading our own deployment, not a third party's site.
entries.notes: The URL sample resolves the route against whichever Orincard deployment is under test; the bytes behind it are the repository file recorded alongside it.

entries.grant: Hostile strings and archives constructed by the team to trip our own guards; free to use anywhere in testing.
entries.notes: Each payload is built to hit a named rejection in archive.ts or safe-fetch.ts. Nothing is lifted from a public exploit corpus, so no upstream licence attaches.

entries.grant: PDF, PPTX, audio and video artefacts produced locally from Orincard's own text; the derived files inherit the source's rights.
entries.notes: Produced with the tools recorded in docs/licenses/parsers.md (poppler, tesseract, ffmpeg, macOS say) and pptxgenjs. Those tool licences cover the software, not the output; the output's rights come from the original text it was rendered from.

entries.grant: No content rights are claimed or needed: these inputs are classified and refused before any byte is fetched.
entries.notes: Covers platform watch pages and SSRF targets. classifyVideoUrl and safeFetch reject them on the address alone, so the corpus holds a URL string and never the material behind it. Recording them as licensed would be false; recording them as unknown would be worse.
